method: Eight parallel reviewers, one per screen family, judged every capture against the SMILE and NMBA designed frames from the MoSJE Portal Handoff file and the written house standard; 261 reviewer findings were consolidated into 30 portal-wide and 63 screen findings. Every Blocker and every portal-wide claim reported by only some reviewers was re-checked on the capture before publication.

globals.title: The whole type scale is 3px larger than the estate's
globals.build: Tailwind's scale is redefined upward: body text renders at 17px on 18,340 elements across 221 of 224 screens, with 15, 19 and 21px elsewhere. None of these sizes is drawn in the handoff file.
globals.fix: Return --text-xs / --text-sm / --text-base to 12 / 14 / 16px (one declaration block); the PROPOSED panel shows the result on this screen.

globals.title: Body and label text uses Tailwind's slate ramp, not the estate's ink
globals.build: Seven slate values (#314158, #4a5565 on all 224 screens, #0f172b, #364153, …) colour the text. The handoff file inks text in #1f2937 / #374151 / #6b7280.
globals.fix: Map the slate steps to #1f2937 (primary), #374151 (secondary) and #6b7280 (supporting); the PROPOSED panel shows the result on this screen.

globals.title: The portal loads none of the design system's tokens
globals.build: 0 --sa-* custom properties on a pre-login and an authenticated screen; the portal declares its own --primary-color: #0a3a74. This is why the type scale and palette drifted.
globals.fix: Load the published token stylesheet and consume --sa-* instead of a private variable set.

globals.title: Status colours come from Tailwind's palette, and one meaning has four greens
globals.build: Errors paint #fb2c36 / #e7000b / #c10007, and 'approved / on track' uses four greens (#008236, #007a55, #00a63e, #006045) across screens.
globals.fix: Use the file's status colours — #ec5042 for error, #2e7d32 for success — and one green for approved / on track.

globals.title: Wide tables run past their card and hide the right-hand columns
globals.build: On list and report screens the table is wider than its card, with no visible scroll cue, so the last columns — often Status, Remarks, dates and the row Actions — are cut off or sit entirely off-screen.
globals.fix: Let the table scroll inside its card with a visible scrollbar and a sticky first column, or drop low-value columns into a row detail; as in SMILE Users, every column including Actions is visible at 1440px.

globals.title: The floating accessibility button covers row actions, figures and form fields
globals.build: The round 'Ctrl+F2' button is fixed mid-right over the content area and sits on top of the last table column, Edit/Delete actions, KPI cards and inputs on screens across every role.
globals.fix: Move it to the bottom-right corner, 32px in, clear of the content column, and pad the content's right edge so nothing sits under it — the estate's corner-rail placement.

globals.title: Inside the portal the masthead is not the estate masthead
globals.build: After sign-in every screen shows the PM-AJAY logo with Swachh Bharat and Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav marks and an unlabelled language glyph; the National Emblem lockup, Digital India and SAMAVESH marks and the English selector the sign-in screen carries are missing.
globals.fix: Use the estate masthead on every screen: Emblem + Department lockup at left, Digital India and SAMAVESH marks at right, and a labelled 'English' language selector — as on the sign-in screen and in the SMILE and NMBA frames.

globals.title: Side navigation has no icons or group headings, and nests three levels deep
globals.build: The menu is a plain text tree: no leading icons, no section headings, long labels wrapping to two lines, and the Ministry menu nests three levels.
globals.fix: Rebuild on the house side navigation: a 24px Material Symbols Rounded icon per item, uppercase group headings, one level of nesting, single-line labels — as in SMILE and NMBA.

globals.title: The side navigation often highlights nothing, or two items at once
globals.build: On add, create, form-detail and report pages no menu item is highlighted; on others both the parent group and the child are highlighted.
globals.fix: Highlight exactly one item — the screen's own entry, or its parent list for add/edit pages — with the house active style (tinted background, navy text, left indicator).

globals.title: Page titles sit in a white card under an uppercase code label, with no breadcrumb
globals.build: Titles are boxed in a bordered card with a small caps label above them that shows internal role or module codes (sometimes the wrong one); there is no breadcrumb, and the header is drawn three different ways.
globals.fix: Use the house page header on the page background: breadcrumb, Title Case H1, one-line description, primary action at right — no card, no code label — as in SMILE Users and NMBA User Management.

globals.title: Primary buttons are green, bright blue or navy, with no consistent hierarchy
globals.build: Main actions (View, Save, Submit, Export) use two or three greens, a bright blue and navy; secondary buttons use three outline styles; Cancel is red on some forms; Reset is pale grey and looks disabled; exports are red and green 'PDF'/'EXCEL' blocks.
globals.fix: One hierarchy everywhere: navy filled primary, navy outline secondary, text-style tertiary; Reset as secondary; one outline 'Export' with a menu — as in SMILE Users and Fund Monitoring.

globals.title: Table headers are drawn three different ways
globals.build: The same kind of table has a solid blue header with white wrapping text on some screens, a light-blue band on others, and no fill on the rest.
globals.fix: Use one table header everywhere — as in SMILE Users: a light neutral header row with single-line, Title Case, semibold labels and a hairline divider.

globals.title: Table cells wrap onto several lines, making rows very tall and uneven
globals.build: Headers, IDs, dates and status badges wrap onto 2–5 lines, so rows run 74–170px tall and break words at hyphens.
globals.fix: Keep cells to one line at a single, consistent row height: truncate long text with a tooltip, set IDs and dates no-wrap, and give badges a fixed single-line width.

globals.title: Row actions are a different control on every list
globals.build: Rows carry a filled blue 'Actions' button on one list, unlabelled pencil/bin icons on another, three coloured buttons on a third, and tiny icon-only reorder/remove controls in repeaters.
globals.fix: Use one row-action pattern: a kebab or 'Actions' menu at the row end, with labelled items and icon buttons at least 24px with accessible names — as in SMILE Users.

globals.title: Pagination is built several ways, with plain 'Show … entries' selects
globals.build: Some tables use old DataTables 'Show 25 entries' and 'Search:' controls, others a native select, others none; wording and placement differ between screens.
globals.fix: Use the house pagination footer on every table: 'Showing 1–10 of N' at left, page-size select and page buttons at right.

globals.title: Search and filters are laid out differently on every list
globals.build: Filters sit in a separate tall card with an empty band beneath, controls are different heights, required asterisks appear on filters that default to 'All', and View/Reset move around.
globals.fix: One toolbar above each table: search at left, filters inline, Reset and the primary action at right, all controls one height, no required markers on filters — as in SMILE Users.

globals.title: Before a search, screens say 'No data' — and empty lists are a bare grey sentence
globals.build: Reports show 'No data available', an empty grey strip or 'Showing 0 to 0 of 0 entries' before the user has run them; an empty checker queue says 'No proposals match your filters' when no filter is set.
globals.fix: Design three states separately: idle ('Choose filters and select View'), empty ('No proposals yet') and filtered-to-nothing ('No results for these filters — Reset'), each with an icon and one line.

globals.title: File uploads and dates are the browser's default controls
globals.build: Uploads show the raw 'Choose File / No file chosen' control and dates the native mm/dd/yyyy picker with a black calendar glyph.
globals.fix: Use the house upload field (drop zone, file-type hint, uploaded-file chip) and the house date field (dd/mm/yyyy, calendar icon) — as in SMILE Add Shelter Home.

globals.title: Form buttons float outside the card and move from form to form
globals.build: Save/Submit/Cancel sit below the card, in a floating summary bar, at left or at right depending on the form; the back action has four labels and three positions.
globals.fix: Put form actions in the card footer, right-aligned — Cancel (secondary) then Save (primary) — and one 'Back' link above the title, as in SMILE Add User.

globals.title: Form sections are headed four different ways
globals.build: Some sections use full-width navy title bars, others solid blue bars, a navy banner as the page title, or a plain card title.
globals.fix: Use the house section label — 16px semibold #1f2937 title with an optional one-line description, inside the card — for every section.

globals.title: Placeholders are dashed, worded five ways, carry rules, and get cut off
globals.build: Select prompts read '-- Select --', 'Select', '--Select State--' and more; validation rules are written as placeholders; values and prompts are truncated mid-word.
globals.fix: Use 'Select <field>' for every select, put rules in helper text under the field, and size fields so their content fits.

globals.title: Headings, labels and column headers are not in Title Case, and some are all capitals
globals.build: Titles, KPI labels, form labels and column headers mix sentence case, ALL CAPS and Title Case; units are written 'Rs' and '₹'.
globals.fix: Title Case for every title, label, column header and button (small words lower-case); no forced capitals; '₹' throughout.
globals.anchorText: PMAGY - WORKS IDENTIFIED PROGRESS REPORT IN VILLAGES

globals.title: The same thing is named differently in the menu, the page title and the report
globals.build: Menu labels, page titles, column names and Format numbers disagree (e.g. 'Create', 'Add' and 'New' for one action; 'Format III(B)' spelled several ways).
globals.fix: Adopt one name per object and action and use it in the menu, the title and the button.

globals.title: KPI cards are styled four ways and crowd their labels
globals.build: Stat cards are fully tinted in yellow/red/green on one dashboard, carry coloured left edges on another, and wrap labels in six-across rows on a third.
globals.fix: One KPI card everywhere — as in SMILE Dashboard: white card with a hairline border and 8px radius, a short label above the figure, an optional trend chip, and no fully tinted backgrounds.

globals.title: Amounts, dates and IDs are formatted several ways
globals.build: Amounts appear with and without digit grouping, dates in three formats (sometimes in one column), and IDs in a monospace font.
globals.fix: Indian digit grouping with '₹' for amounts, dd/mm/yyyy for dates, and Noto Sans tabular figures for IDs.

globals.title: Read-only and calculated fields look editable
globals.build: Locked fields are styled two ways, and on some forms they look identical to editable inputs.
globals.fix: One read-only style: a quiet neutral fill (#f9fafb), no focus ring, and 'Auto-calculated' helper text where the value is derived.

globals.title: Dashboards explain how to use themselves
globals.build: Subtitles and dotted notes tell the reader how to read the cards and charts.
globals.fix: Remove the instructions; a chart that needs them has a legend problem. Keep a one-line factual description.
globals.anchorText: Showing . Each number is clickable — it opens the state-wise break-up with the d

globals.title: Scheme dashboards have no page title
globals.build: The GIA, Hostel and Adarsh Gram dashboards open straight into cards with no title or description.
globals.fix: Add the house page header — Title Case title and a one-line description — as on the Ministry dashboards.

globals.title: A pale-blue scrollbar sliver is always visible beside the side menu
globals.build: A thin blue bar shows at the menu's right edge on every screen, even when nothing scrolls.
globals.fix: Hide the scrollbar until the menu overflows, and use the thin neutral overlay scrollbar when it does.

globals.title: The footer credits UX4G, not the Department, and has no Terms, Privacy or Help links
globals.build: Every signed-in screen ends with '© 2025 - Copyright UX4G. All rights reserved. Powered by NeGD | MeitY Government of India®2025 UX4G' and no Terms & Conditions, Privacy Policy or Help links.
globals.fix: Use the estate footer: '© Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, Government of India' with Terms & Conditions, Privacy Policy and Help links — the GIGW 3.0 mandatory set.

screen.title: The password form's only button says 'Send OTP'
screen.build: After Email Id/Username and Password, the primary button reads 'Send OTP', and there is no alternative sign-in route. SMILE sign-in has 'Log In' plus a secondary 'Sign in with OTP'.
screen.fix: Confirm this is intended (password then OTP as a second step). If it is, keep it; otherwise label the button 'Log In', as in SMILE Sign-in.

screen.title: Sign-in heading and links are centred and oversized compared with the reference
screen.build: 'Log In to your account' is a centred 28px bold heading in mixed case, the terms line is centred and breaks 'Terms of Use' across two lines, and the hero line 'Justice. Equality. Dignity.' is 48px.
screen.fix: Left-align the form block as in SMILE Sign-in (heading about 20px, 'Log In to Your Account'), keep the terms link on one line, and bring the hero line down to the reference's weight.

screen.title: Ministry dashboard charts reuse colours with different meanings
screen.build: Brown means "Declared", "PMAGY", "Yet To Start", "Gap-filling Funds", "Draft", "Estimation" and "Non-Saturated" in different charts. "Utilization" is green in one pie and blue in the pie next to it. Households Survey colours three plain categories as if they were separate series.
screen.fix: Fix one meaning per colour across the dashboard (e.g. completed/utilised = one colour, pending/yet to start = another), and use a single colour for non-series bars, as in the SMILE dashboard Age Distribution.

screen.title: Chart text is not Noto Sans, state labels are clipped, and pies show no values
screen.build: Chart axis and legend text uses a generic system sans, not Noto Sans. State names on the Infrastructure Work Information x-axis are rotated 45° and clipped ("RNATAKA", "MIL NADU"). The pie and donut charts show no percentages or values.
screen.fix: Set the chart library font to Noto Sans at 12px. Use a horizontal bar chart for 10 states so names read in full. Show percentages on slices and values in the legend, as in the SMILE dashboard Gender Distribution.

screen.title: Ministry Manage UC shows 25 rows while the page-size control says 10
screen.build: The footer reads "Showing 1 to 25 of 131" and the table shows 25 rows, but the "Show [10] entries" select still says 10.
screen.fix: Keep the page-size select and the rendered rows in sync (default 10, as in SMILE Users "Showing 10 of 1248 items").

screen.title: The Dashboard shows the same four figures twice in each section
screen.build: In 'Adarsh Gram Progress' and 'Financial Progress', four KPI cards are followed by a bar list repeating the same four values with the same labels.
screen.fix: Show each figure once: keep the KPI cards and turn the bars into a percentage-only funnel, or drop the cards, as SMILE Dashboard does with KPIs in one band and charts that add new breakdowns.

screen.title: Side-by-side cards are stretched to equal height, leaving large blank areas
screen.build: 'Allocation by Scheme Component' is stretched to match 'Requires Attention' and is more than half empty. The same happens with 'Hostel Funds (₹ Cr)' next to 'Construction Snapshot' and with 'Gap-Filling Funds' on Adarsh Gram.
screen.fix: Balance the pair (give the shorter card a chart or more content, or change the column split), or let each card size to its content, as SMILE Dashboard's chart cards do.

screen.title: Summary banners use a success style for poor results and print 'N/A' in a sentence
screen.build: Financial Management shows a green banner with a tick for 'PFMS transaction success at 27%' and 'Average release-to-utilisation time has improved to N/A.' The banner colour is fixed per page (green, blue or red) and does not reflect whether the figure is good or bad.
screen.fix: Set the banner tone from the figure against its target (success, warning or error), and leave out any sentence whose value is missing instead of printing 'N/A'.
screen.anchorText: Average release-to-utilisation time has improved to N/A.

screen.title: Beneficiary/SHG Report has no menu entry, so nothing is highlighted on that page
screen.build: On Beneficiary/SHG Report the GIA Report menu stays collapsed with no active item for any role; the report is not listed in the GIA Report submenu.
screen.fix: Add "Beneficiary/SHG Report" to the GIA Report submenu and highlight it when open — as the active "Committee Reports" item in NMBA Committee Reports.

screen.title: Two reports show only the first 10 rows with no way to see the rest
screen.build: Capacity Building & IEC ends with "Showing 10 of 27819 entries" and no page controls; Project Status shows 10 rows with no footer at all. A Ministry user cannot reach any other record.
screen.fix: Add the house pagination footer — numbered pages with previous/next, a "Showing [10] of N items" page-size select — as under the tables in SMILE Users and NMBA Committee Reports.

screen.title: Ministry Perspective Plan Summary opens with "Failed to load data." in red
screen.build: For the Ministry the result area shows plain red "Failed to load data." with a red underlined "Retry" link, before any filter is chosen; the four state and district role copies load the summary table.
screen.fix: Confirm why the Ministry request fails and fix it. Replace the raw red line with a designed error state: an icon, one sentence in #1f2937 ink, and a secondary "Try Again" button, centred in the card.

screen.title: Ministry State Projects Summary is an unpaged 39,000px table whose last column is cut off
screen.build: For the Ministry every district of every state is rendered in one table (~39,400px page), so Grand Total is only reachable after a very long scroll, and the "Total Amount (Lakh)" column runs past the card edge and is clipped. The state-role copies show one state and fit.
screen.fix: Show one row per state with the districts behind an expand or a state filter, or page the table, and keep all columns inside the card — as the ranked, paged tables in SMILE Performance Statistics. Put Grand Total where it is visible without scrolling.

screen.title: State name is centred vertically in a cell spanning all its districts
screen.build: Each state name sits in the vertical middle of a merged cell up to ~1,000px tall, so a reader scrolling the district rows cannot see which state they belong to.
screen.fix: Top-align the state name in its merged cell (or repeat it as a group header row) so it stays with the first district row.

screen.title: 'Generate Sanction' page is actually a sanction-orders list
screen.build: The page is titled 'Generate Sanction' but shows a 'Sanction Orders' table, with a second 'Generate Sanction' button and an outlined 'Back to Dashboard' beside it. The first row's Document cell shows an empty grey pill where other rows show 'View'.
screen.fix: Title the page 'Sanction Orders', keep 'Generate Sanction' as its only primary action, and confirm 'Back to Dashboard' is intended. Show '—' plainly in empty cells.

screen.title: Attention and snapshot lists flag zero-value items and use mismatched status chips
screen.build: 'Requires Attention' lists items like '0 audit observations open — Track' and '0 UCs pending over 90 days — Review'. Snapshot cards pair '0 hostels completed' with 'On track' and '0 under construction' with 'Active'. Green chips read '0 over 90 days' and 'avg 0-day slip'.
screen.fix: Show only items that need attention, and give the card a designed empty state ('No items need attention') when none do. Use one status set (e.g. On Track / Monitor / Action) whose meaning matches the figure.

screen.title: Bar charts label some bars and clip labels inside short bars
screen.build: In the fund pipelines, the value sits inside the bar, so on a short bar it is clipped (GIA 'Funds utilised' shows a cut-off '₹587'). On Executive Summary, the full-width Sanction and Release bars have no value at all.
screen.fix: Put every value label at the end of its bar, outside when the bar is too short, and label all bars the same way, as in SMILE Dashboard's Age Distribution chart.

screen.title: "Not Uploaded" is faint two-line grey text beside a "View" link
screen.build: The Completion Certificate column shows "Not Uploaded" in light grey wrapped over two lines, with no chip, next to rows that show a blue "View" link.
screen.fix: Show a neutral "Not Uploaded" chip on one line and a labelled "View Certificate" link, so both states read as designed values.

screen.title: Hostel UC List hides its approve and reject buttons off the right edge
screen.build: The table is about 2,100px wide inside a 1,117px card: Download UC/Interest is cut in half and UC/Interest Status, UC Status, Remarks, Created Date and the round approve/reject buttons sit beyond the screen, with no visible scroll bar. The page description tells the Ministry to approve or reject from a column they cannot see.
screen.fix: Fit the table to the card as in SMILE Users: drop or merge low-value columns (Category, Remarks), keep amounts on one line, and pin a labelled Actions column to the right edge with Approve / Reject as text buttons in a row menu.

screen.title: A wrapping label pushes one select out of line on Institute Registration
screen.build: 'Administrative Department Name' wraps to two lines, so its select sits about 22px lower than its neighbours. Correspondence Address is a narrow single-line input for a 10–200 character address.
screen.fix: Keep labels to one line (shorten to 'Administrative Department') or align fields to the row baseline, and make the address a full-width multi-line field with a helper line for the length rule, as in SMILE Shelter Homes Add.

screen.title: The six admin lists are built three different ways
screen.build: User Management puts a navy 'Add User' in the header with a count, search, Reset and a labelled filter row. Role Management has no header action, a full-width pill-shaped search outside the card with 'Add Role' beside it, and no count or Reset. Courses, Domains, Sub Domains and Institutes use green 'Export' and 'Add…'/'Create' buttons.
screen.fix: Build all admin lists from one template as in SMILE Users: header with primary action top-right, one toolbar (search + filter dropdowns) above the table, table and pagination in one card.

screen.title: Two-line labels push their fields down, so a row of fields no longer lines up
screen.build: In Personal Details, 'Does the beneficiary fall under the BPL Category?' and 'Annual Family Income Group' wrap to two lines. Their dropdowns start 21px lower than Occupation and Physically Challenged in the same row, and the Annual Family Income asterisk sits alone on the second line.
screen.fix: Shorten the labels ('BPL Category', 'Annual Family Income') or top-align every field in a row to the tallest label, as in SMILE Add Shelter Homes where each row of inputs shares one baseline.
screen.anchorText: Does the beneficiary fall under the BPL Category?

screen.title: Address boxes start lower than the field beside them and have a different corner radius
screen.build: 'Address of Executing Agency' starts 10px below the neighbouring Name input, although both labels share a line. The address boxes have 5px corners while other inputs have 8px.
screen.fix: Remove the extra top margin on multi-line fields so they align with their row, and use the 8px input radius.

screen.title: Income Generation card uses a dollar-sign icon in a multi-coloured icon set
screen.build: The intervention cards use blue, orange and green filled tiles, and Income Generation Activity shows a '$' icon on an Indian scheme priced in rupees.
screen.fix: Use Material Symbols Rounded 'currency_rupee' (weight 300) and one neutral or navy tile colour for all three intervention cards.

screen.title: Internal codes and system notes are shown to users
screen.build: The tutoring footer reads 'Total Project Cost · type 6'. Screens also carry 'Optional · not stored on server', the pill 'Achieved pending — progress reporting not yet enabled', and 'Computed live as you fill in the form.'. The total cost appears twice on the tutoring form.
screen.fix: Remove internal codes and system notes from the screen. Show the achieved figure as '—' with no banner, and show the total once (in the footer band).

screen.title: Yes/No and Rural/Urban switches barely show which option is chosen
screen.build: The selected option is only a white chip on a light-grey track with the same dark text, so 'Yes' and 'No' look almost identical. On Level of Project neither State nor District looks selected.
screen.fix: Mark the selected option clearly: navy fill with white text, or a navy border and text, and default the switch to a real value or show 'Select' as unselected.

screen.title: District Maker dashboard shows 'Approved — 2' under cards that say Approved 0 and Sanctioned 2
screen.build: The Approved Projects card reads 0 and Sanctioned Projects reads 2, but the Processing split bar and its legend label the same two projects 'Approved — 2' in green. A reader sees two different answers for how many projects are approved.
screen.fix: Label and colour the split from the same statuses as the cards, as the State Maker and State Checker dashboards already do ('Sanctioned — N'), so every figure on the page comes from one reading.
screen.note: Downgraded from Blocker: the bar's 'Approved' may include sanctioned projects — confirm before treating it as a data error.

screen.title: District and state users can open reports their menu does not offer
screen.build: District maker and district checker menus list five reports, yet State Projects Summary, Perspective Plan, UC, Uploaded Beneficiary Data and both Beneficiary reports open for them by address with no menu item highlighted; state maker and checker menus omit Beneficiary Status and UC, which also open.
screen.fix: Confirm which reports each role is meant to see. Either list them in that role’s GIA Report menu (and highlight the active one) or block the route for that role.

screen.title: 'Draft' is shown as a red badge, the same family as 'Rejected'
screen.build: Draft records get a red-tinted badge, and a solid red badge means Rejected on the same table. On this estate red means a rejected application, so a draft reads as a failure.
screen.fix: Show Draft in a neutral grey badge (#f9fafb fill, #374151 text, #d1d5db border). Keep #ec5042 red for Rejected only.

screen.title: Menu item under 'Manage Institute' is labelled 'Pending Project'
screen.build: On the Pending Institutes screen the active menu item under Manage Institute reads 'Pending Project', which is also the name of the item under Manage GIA Project. Two menu entries share a name but open different lists.
screen.fix: Rename it 'Pending Institutes', to match the page title and the State Checker menu ('Pending Institute').

screen.title: Three scheme landing addresses open a bare 404 page with no header, menu or footer
screen.build: /state/gia, /state/hos and /state/hos-checker render only a centred '404 / Page Not Found' card with a Go Back button — no masthead, side menu or footer, and no way into the scheme.
screen.fix: Redirect each scheme landing to that role's scheme dashboard, and draw any remaining not-found state inside the portal shell (masthead, side menu, footer) so the user keeps their navigation.

screen.title: The pending-projects list has a different title, filters and columns for each role
screen.build: The same list is titled 'Pending Projects' (District Maker, State Checker), 'Pending Project List' (State Maker), 'Project List' (District Checker) and 'All Project List' (Ministry). The filter order swaps Status and Financial Year, the Status filter is called 'Bucket' for District Checker, and the export is green 'Export', outlined 'Export CSV' or missing. The columns also differ: District Maker shows Project/FY/District/Documents, while State Maker shows S. No./Project Id/State/Created at.
screen.fix: Use one list template, as the SMILE Users and Roles screens share one: the same title pattern, filter order (Status, Financial Year, Type of Intervention, Search), export button and core columns, adding only the columns a role needs.

screen.title: The GIA dashboard is built four different ways across the four roles
screen.build: Across the four roles the same seven cards change order (Returned and Rejected swap places) and colour: Pending is yellow for makers but white for checkers, and Forwarded is white for District Maker but green for District Checker. The State Checker renames Forwarded to 'Approved / Forwarded'. District Checker has no 'Application Status' panel, approval rate or processing split, and only the makers get a 'Filters' heading and Export.
screen.fix: Build one dashboard template for all four roles. Keep the same card order, names and colours, and drop only the cards a role cannot act on. Confirm the District Checker's default '2026-2027' year filter (others default to All) is intended.

screen.title: Funds column says "₹ in Lakhs" but shows full rupee figures without grouping
screen.build: Values such as 18000000 and 30000000 appear under a header that says the unit is lakhs, and no screen groups the digits, while the UC List formats the same kind of figure as ₹ 1,62,50,000.
screen.fix: Convert to the stated unit or change the header to "(₹)", right-align, and use Indian digit grouping everywhere, as the UC List already does.
screen.anchorText: Funds proposed under PMAJAY (₹ in Lakhs)

screen.title: Refresh button drops below the filter row, and a stray "all" label floats in the table header
screen.build: On Maker Pending Proposals, Refresh sits 26px lower than the selects and Export beside it, and the table title row ends with a lone lowercase "all" at the right.
screen.fix: Align all toolbar controls to one baseline and remove the "all" text (or turn it into a proper filter chip).

screen.title: Checker Pending Hostel List shows a count of 0 above three rows, and has no pagination
screen.build: The count chip beside the table title reads 0 while three pending hostels are listed. The table also ends without the "Showing 1 to n of n" and pagination footer every other list carries.
screen.fix: Bind the chip to the same result count the table renders, and add the standard footer (range text left, pages and page size right) as in SMILE Users.

screen.title: "Implementing Agency" column shows Boys / Girls
screen.build: The column headed Implementing Agency contains the hostel category (Boys, Girls) or a dash, never an agency name.
screen.fix: Either show the implementing agency in this column or rename it to Hostel Category, and use the same header on every hostel table.

screen.title: Uneven vertical spacing between form rows
screen.build: On Submit Hostel UC the gap between rows 1 and 2 is about 44px but between rows 2 and 3 about 16px; on Add Sanctioned Hostel the two-line 'Per Inmate Maximum Admissible Amount (₹)' label pushes its field about 20px below its neighbours.
screen.fix: Use one 24px row gap (house spacing step) as in SMILE Onboard New User, and shorten the long label so all fields in a row align.

screen.title: Checker sees the same 'Submit Hostel UC' action and form as the maker
screen.build: Every other create action (Create Proposal, Add Sanctioned Hostel, Submit Progress) is removed for the checker, but UC submission is offered identically to both roles.
screen.fix: Confirm this is intended; if the checker only verifies UCs, replace the button with a review action and remove Submit Hostel UC from the checker's menu.

screen.title: Error toast covers the masthead controls and repeats the inline alert
screen.build: The "already declared Adarsh Gram" toast is pinned over the top-right of the masthead, hiding text-size, contrast, language and the user profile, while the same message is also shown as a red alert inside the form.
screen.fix: Show the message once, as the inline alert at the top of the form; if a toast is kept, position it below the masthead (top 140px) using the .Toast Status component.
screen.anchorText: This village is already a declared Adarsh Gram — Format-I cannot be submitted.

screen.title: Create Format II has no Submit or Cancel button, and its fields sit off the grid
screen.build: The form ends after "Monitorable Indicator" with no action buttons visible; the helper text under Domain pushes the Monitorable Indicator field onto its own row after a ~70px gap.
screen.fix: Show Cancel and Submit (disabled until valid) at the bottom of the card as on Format III(A) Create — confirm whether they only appear after selection; move the helper text below both selects or into a tooltip so the row stays aligned.

screen.title: Tables run past the card edge, hiding the Delete and Action columns
screen.build: On Manage Household the last column is cut off at 1440px: the header reads "A" and every Delete button shows only "De". On Format VII the officers table clips "Pin Code" and its Action column (starting at x 1458) is entirely off-screen.
screen.fix: Fit the table inside its card: put row actions in a narrow Actions column of icon buttons (edit, delete) as in SMILE Users, and wrap long headers; if columns still exceed the width, let the table scroll inside the card with the Actions column pinned right.

screen.title: Format III(B) list shows no table and no prompt
screen.build: The screen shows only the location, domain and indicator selectors; below them the page is empty, with no results table, empty state or instruction telling the user to choose a domain and indicator.
screen.fix: Show the results table area with a designed idle state ("Select a Domain and Monitorable Indicator to see records") and, once filtered, a "No records found" empty state; place Back top-right as on the other screens.

screen.title: Format IV new entry mixes label-above and label-left layouts and shifts its grid
screen.build: The first section uses labels above fields in 3 columns, then 2 columns, then full width; the funds section switches to labels on the left with inputs pushed to the right column, leaving the middle empty on several rows.
screen.fix: Use one form grid with labels above, as in SMILE Add User: a 2-column (or 3-column) grid with 24px gutter throughout, grouping "Name of Scheme" + "Funds Allocated" as a paired row.
screen.anchorText: Estimated Cost in Rs (As provided by concerned authority)

screen.title: Required asterisks wrap onto their own line
screen.build: The red asterisk drops below the label on "Central Govt. Scheme (other than PMAGY)" and "Agency / Department for Implementation", and below the column title in the Format I member table ("Name", "Designation", "Mobile Number") and Format VII "Pin Code".
screen.fix: Keep the asterisk inline with the last word (non-breaking) as in SMILE Add User "Full Name *", and shorten or widen the labels so they sit on one line.

screen.title: Score of 0 is shown in the same green as full marks
screen.build: In the "Score achieved" column every value is green, so an indicator scoring 0 looks as successful as one scoring 2.
screen.fix: Show scores in neutral #1f2937 text, or use a Badge with success (#2e7d32) only for full score and error (#ec5042) for 0, as the house status palette defines.

screen.title: Format VI renders a 5,000px table with no way to keep the headers in view
screen.build: All ten domains and 50+ indicators are in one table running to 5,472px; once scrolled, the column headers (Benchmark, Scoring System, Status, Score achieved) are no longer visible.
screen.fix: Make the header row sticky, or split the table into collapsible per-domain sections with a domain subtotal, so the reader always knows which column is which.

screen.title: Manage MoM uses a different, centred narrow layout from every other screen
screen.build: Content starts at x 473 in a 768px centred column, while all other screens start at x 298 and fill the width; it has no title card, no back action, and its action bar is a separate floating card.
screen.fix: Lay it out on the same full-width content column (left edge aligned with the other screens, 24px gutter) and the same page header pattern, with "Replace Files" top-right as in SMILE Users.

screen.title: All Reports is two text links in a mostly empty page
screen.build: The hub has one navy-headed card containing two blue text links with no description or icon; the rest of the page is empty.
screen.fix: Present each report as a Link-Card with an icon, title and one-line description in a card grid, as the estate's Link-Card component does.

screen.title: Report tables have no search, filter or export
screen.build: Households Details and Deleted Households show the table directly under the title with no search bar, filters or Export action.
screen.fix: Show a search bar above the table and an Export button top-right, as in NMBA Committee Reports.

screen.title: Report tables show Category as a number and "Deleted By" as an ID
screen.build: Households Details and Deleted Households list Category as "1", "2", "3" and Deleted By as "44", while Manage Survey shows the same field as "SC", "ST", "Others".
screen.fix: Display the category name (SC / ST / Others) and the deleting user's name, matching Manage Survey.

screen.title: Format VII inputs have teal borders unlike every other form
screen.build: All text inputs on Format VII have a teal outline (reading as a validated state) and 4px radius, while other forms use grey #d1d5db borders and 6px radius; the textarea uses yet another grey.
screen.fix: Use the input-field/text default: 1px #d1d5db border, 8px radius, 40px height; reserve colour borders for focus and error states.

screen.title: Village screen is titled "Reporting Format for District"
screen.build: The village-role Format VII page is headed "Reporting Format for District" and asks for "Details of district level officers" and district committee meetings.
screen.fix: Confirm this is intended for the village role; if so, say so in the description line, otherwise retitle to the village-level format.
screen.anchorText: Format VII – Reporting Format for District

screen.title: Format IV entry form uses navy section bars and side labels unlike every other form
screen.build: Sections open with full-width dark navy bars ('Location & Work Identification', 'Details of scheme…'). The funding section switches to labels on the left with inputs on the right, where the other forms use white card headers and labels above fields. On long labels the red required star drops onto its own line ('Central Govt. Scheme (other than PMAGY)', 'Agency / Department for Implementation').
screen.fix: Use the section headers from SMILE Shelter Homes Add (uppercase 14px title with a hairline rule) and labels above fields throughout, keeping the star on the label's last line. Likely shared with the village role's Format IV.
screen.anchorText: Details of scheme from where funds are being sourced

screen.title: Format IV step tabs are heavy filled blocks with a focus ring left on the active step
screen.build: Estimation / Release / Utilization / Work Progress are four 269px filled blocks. The active step is solid navy with a visible focus outline at rest; the others are grey with numbered circles.
screen.fix: Use the library's step/type-2 stepper (numbered circle, label, connector line) for the four stages, with the focus ring shown only on keyboard focus.

screen.title: Declaration Requests shows 18 rows while the page size says 10
screen.build: The 'Show 10 entries' selector is set to 10, yet all 18 rows render on one page and the footer reads 'Showing 1 to 18 of 18'. The page runs to 2,100px.
screen.fix: Honour the page size (10 rows, pages 1–2) and use the pagination from SMILE Users: page numbers left, 'Showing [10] of N items' right.

screen.title: All Reports is a plain link list under navy bars, with a misspelt all-caps heading
screen.build: Reports are grouped under full-width dark navy bars, and each report is a bare text link with no icon or description. One heading reads 'VILLAGE DEVELOPEMENT PLAN' (misspelt, all caps) where the others are Title Case. Link labels mix cases ('Works in progress', 'Duplicate name in 3 A').
screen.fix: Correct to 'Village Development Plan'. Use the section-title style from SMILE Shelter Homes Add for group headings and the library Link-Card (icon, Title Case name, one-line description) for each report.

screen.title: Format VII officers table hides the required Pin Code and delete columns off the right edge
screen.build: The district officers table is wider than its card: Office Address is cut at the card edge and the required Pin Code column and the row delete button sit entirely outside the visible area, while the footer says 'Complete all mandatory fields to enable Submit.' A user cannot see the field that keeps Submit disabled.
screen.fix: Lay each officer out as a row of fields in the card's 3-column grid (as in SMILE Shelter Homes Add, fields wrap to the next row) or cut the table to columns that fit 1116px; never put a required field behind a hidden horizontal scroll.

screen.title: User Management is built on a different list template from the rest of the role
screen.build: The other lists put a count title and search inside the table card. Here a short pill-shaped search floats on the page above it, the primary 'Add User' is dark navy with no icon, and row actions are an orange pencil and a red bin with no button frame. Role ('AG Village') and Jurisdiction wrap to two lines.
screen.fix: Match NMBA User Management: full-width search bar with an 'All States/UTs' filter above the table, 'Add User +' top-right, and row actions as 32px outlined icon buttons (neutral pencil, red bin) with accessible labels.

screen.title: With Language set to "All", FAQ lists Hindi and English versions of each question together, with a "Question: 1 :" prefix
screen.build: With "All" selected, Hindi and English versions of the same questions alternate in one list, and every item begins "Question: N :".
screen.fix: Default the language filter to the interface language so each question appears once, and drop the "Question: N :" prefix (a plain ordered accordion is enough).

screen.title: Format VIII lists Uttar Pradesh districts for an Andhra Pradesh user
screen.build: The form is locked to "ANDHRA PRADESH - 28", but section 6b "No. of key personnel of the Districts trained so far" lists 75 Uttar Pradesh districts (Agra to Varanasi) for data entry.
screen.fix: Load the district rows for the logged-in state (Andhra Pradesh has 26, as the Financial Progress tab shows), and verify the state filter on this query before release.

screen.title: Unbuilt pages show "Coming Soon" or "will be implemented later" to users
screen.build: Funds and Monitoring show a card saying "Coming Soon / This section is under development", and the Format VIII State/UT report says "This report will be implemented later." Funds and Monitoring are not highlighted in the side navigation.
screen.fix: Remove unbuilt pages from navigation and report links until they exist. If one must stay, use one designed empty state (icon, Title Case heading, one plain sentence) with the same wording on every page.

screen.title: Media gallery rows are 300px+ tall because location details are stacked in one cell
screen.build: The "Geographical Info" column stacks up to nine labelled lines (Selection Year, State, District, Block, Gram Panchayat, Village, Work Type, Monitorable Indicator, Action Plan) in each row, so only about three records fit on screen.
screen.fix: Keep rows near the SMILE Users 56px height: show Village and District in the cell, and move the rest to a row detail drawer or a "View Details" action.

screen.title: Most media rows show a grey placeholder icon instead of a thumbnail
screen.build: In the Image/Video column, most rows show a generic grey picture icon, and only the first row shows a real thumbnail. Nothing tells the user whether the file is missing or still loading.
screen.fix: Show a real thumbnail or video frame. Where none exists, use a designed "Preview Unavailable" tile that differs clearly from a loading skeleton.
